data.about: A cantilever truss on a wall: a horizontal roller at the top, a pin at the bottom, five equal loads on the top chord. A trial funicular polygon finds the resultant; where its line of action crosses the roller's horizontal, the three-force rule fixes the pin direction and closes the load line: reactions A, B_H, B_V. The force diagram is then constructed joint by joint in Bow's notation (points 1…7), and flipping the diagonals rebuilds it — swapping tension (pink) and compression (blue) in diagonals and verticals.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: top chord on the roller B, bottom chord on the pin A, tip C (drag all three!); verticals and diagonals divide it into four panels — the "flip diagonals" toggle mirrors the diagonals
steps.title: A cantilever truss on the wall

steps.caption: left: F₁ … F₅ act on the top-chord joints — right: stacked tip-to-tail on the load line (Bow's notation: b, c, d, e, f between the loads)
steps.title: Five equal loads

steps.caption: right: any trial pole o with rays to the load points — left: a trial funicular from N₁, one string per panel, parallel to the rays
steps.title: A trial funicular

steps.caption: left: the outer strings (dashed), extended, meet at S₁: R acts on the vertical through S₁ (dashed green, drag it) — right: R = the whole load line
steps.title: The resultant R

steps.caption: left: the roller at B can only push horizontally; that line meets R's line of action at A₂ — so the pin reaction at A must point along A–A₂ — right: the parallel through the load-line end meets the roller's horizontal at the closing point Z
steps.title: The three-force rule

steps.caption: right: roller A = Z→top (drawn on its line), pin = bottom→Z split into B_V (beside) and B_H (above) — left: the wall pushes at B and at A (green arrows)
steps.title: The reactions A, B_H, B_V

steps.caption: the first support joint closes: the wall member 15 with its chord partner — right: from Z, parallel to the wall → Bow point 1
steps.title: Joint by joint — point 1

steps.caption: the other support joint closes: diagonal 13 and the remaining chord — right: parallels through the load point and point 1 → point 2
steps.title: Point 2 — the first diagonal

steps.caption: the next joint closes with vertical 11 and a chord piece — right: the vertical through point 2 meets the chord parallel → point 3
steps.title: Point 3 — the first vertical

steps.caption: diagonal 9 and its chord partner — right: parallels meet at point 4
steps.title: Point 4 — the second diagonal

steps.caption: vertical 7 and a chord piece → point 5
steps.title: Point 5 — the second vertical

steps.caption: diagonal 5 and its chord partner → point 6
steps.title: Point 6 — the third diagonal

steps.caption: vertical 3 and top chord 1 close the joint before the tip → point 7
steps.title: Point 7 — the last panel

steps.caption: left: the last chord piece 2 — right: its force must run from point 7 exactly back to the load-line end: the Cremona diagram closes (the check!)
steps.title: The tip closes the diagram

steps.caption: members resolve pink = tension (top chord, verticals) and blue = compression (bottom chord, diagonals) — FLIP THE DIAGONALS and watch them swap; pipes ∝ force; click a joint for its equilibrium
steps.title: Tension and compression
